plan.title: Author the gate plan
plan.imperative: Map-first: BEFORE authoring execute.json, produce a mission frame from the map input the context step resolved, using templates/MISSION_FRAME.template.md (intent; affected capabilities; relevant examples/events; structural anchors; governing constraints/assumptions; decision anchors and decision pressure; claims/evidence surfaces; map confidence/staleness/disputes; out of scope). Write it to .agent-work/epic-567-door/cmdr-a/MISSION_FRAME.md — that exact path is what the c6 gate reads, so a frame parked anywhere else reads as no frame at all. For a trivial local/mechanical change where the map adds nothing, shrink or skip the frame and say so in its intent; c6 is waivable, so take that escape as a RECORDED waiver (<engine> waive plan --cond c6 --authority human --reason '...') rather than as a silent skip. The c6 gate runs map_orient.py verify-frame over that file: every anchor id the frame cites must exist in the map inventory the context step resolved, or — when context came back DEGRADED — must be one of the substitutes the receipt hash-pinned there, so the frame is compared against a committed prior declaration instead of a same-breath assertion. Know what that check is and is not, and do not overclaim it: it is a regression floor so map-IGNORING cannot silently return, not the fix for map-LATENESS. Measured against this epic's baseline five runs it has sensitivity 0/4 and specificity 0/1, and it inherits the late-anchor defect it was built next to, because anchors-in-a-late-frame is compliance without sequence. The load-bearing map-first anchor is at the context step ('before you open any source file'), which is why verify-orientation is gated there and verify-frame is gated only here. Do NOT 'fix' that asymmetry by also running verify-frame at context: no frame exists at context — the step runs before understand and plan — and the only way to make it pass there is to let an ABSENT frame pass, which is exactly the refusal the whole check is built on. If verify-frame ever has to be context-safe, give it a step-scoped mode; never a vacuous pass. For any low-confidence/stale/disputed map area the run depends on, alter the plan accordingly: add a scout/verification gate or surface it to the human as a decision — never author gates that silently trust an unverified map. Surface durable-structure choices as decision candidates per the skill's Decision candidates section rather than choosing alone. Then author the gate plan into execute.json: each gate the smallest reasonable bite, with close criteria, required evidence, and an anchors block cut from the frame. Before the plan-approved checkpoint run plan-alternatives (parallel gate-plan candidates under distinct constraints, via the references/design-it-twice-brief.md contract) and a cold plan critic (reads the candidate plan + mission frame only, no authoring context); both bias-to-yes — any skip is surfaced as a named untaken road — and the panel-vs-single choice is surfaced to the human at plan approval. In delegated mode, satisfy c3 (plan approved) by attaching a user-decision evidence item citing the launch order's frozen plan and scope -- by default via the spine_evidence MCP tool (action=attach, task_id=plan, evidence_type=user-decision, fields={cite: 'LAUNCH_ORDER:Mission'}); CLI fallback: attach plan --type user-decision --field cite='LAUNCH_ORDER:Mission'; surface a plan-invalidating discovery to the Admiral rather than blocking on the human. execute.context_headroom_note: #467. Absolute-token context reserve for THIS gate only: the engine subtracts it from both the soft and hard caps before dividing by the model's window, so `execute` may not be BEGUN with less than this much room left below the hard cap. It makes the imperative's existing prose instruction ('ensure context headroom before entering') enforceable, and it can only ever tighten -- no gate can raise a threshold. WHY 30000, and it is a GUESS, revisable in place: `execute` is the run's longest gate and the one that cannot be abandoned halfway, because it drives every crew gate and each crew dispatch costs tens of thousands of tokens. The only observation available was a commander sitting at ~127K fill after a cold resume plus one full three-task gate -- which bounds one gate's marginal cost in the tens of thousands but cannot separate it from the resume baseline. 30K is a round number at the low end of that range: on claude-opus-5 (1M window, 80K soft / 150K hard) it moves execute's begin-work line from 15% to 12% and its advisory from 8% to 5%, while every other gate keeps the shipped default. The named settle experiment (read fill_fraction across completed commander runs at the moment execute was started) is NOT runnable from existing artifacts -- gauge.json keeps only the latest reading and the per-gate context manifests record no fill -- so a later run may revise this number here, in this one place, without re-deriving anything.

feedback.title: Record workflow feedback
feedback.imperative: Before committing, reflect honestly on how this run actually went: how closely you followed the skills, handoffs, and checklists; where you had to improvise or work around the instructions; what was ambiguous, missing, or contradictory; and what would have helped. Include the crew Workflow Feedback harvested at each gN-integrate. A 'none' answer requires a run-specific reason ('none — confirmed after review: <what you checked>'); a bare 'none' does not close this step. Then record what happened as EPISODES: one episode per distinct thing that happened — not one per run, and not a summary — each stating its task-intent, expected-behavior, observed-behavior, impact-cost and workaround. An episode is a record, not a rule: write what you observed, and do NOT write a rule for a future agent to follow — a rule to follow belongs in docs/agents/* and is a human's call. Write the delta to .agent-work/epic-567-door/cmdr-a/episode-delta.json and apply it deterministically: py /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/apply_episode_delta.py --delta .agent-work/epic-567-door/cmdr-a/episode-delta.json --store-root episodes. Pass --store-root on every invocation: the writer's default resolves relative to the installed skill directory, so an installed copy would silently build a store at ~/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/episodes — outside the repo — while every gate reported green. Never hand-edit a file under episodes/: that writer is the only write path into it. Then run the capture gate before advancing: py /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/verify_episode_captured.py epic-567-door/cmdr-a --store-root episodes --phase feedback.

archive.title: Archive, commit, and push
archive.imperative: Commit all remaining work, including this run's episodes under episodes/. That is a tracked repo-root path, so the committed episode IS the durable record: it survives `git worktree remove` and lands in a fresh clone. None of the old is-.agent-work-gitignored reasoning applies to it. Push the branch to remote. When you open a PR on Windows, write the body to a temp file and use gh pr create -F <file> — a bash heredoc and a PowerShell @'...'@ here-string both fail for gh pr create --body (here-strings work for git commit -m, not PR bodies). Move .agent-work/epic-567-door/cmdr-a/ to .agent-work/archive/<date>-epic-567-door/cmdr-a/. Run the archive-phase capture gate before marking archive complete — it additionally requires git to TRACK the episode, which is what proves the record outlived this worktree: py /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-commander/scripts/verify_episode_captured.py epic-567-door/cmdr-a --store-root episodes --phase archive. Confirm the branch is clean and merge-ready per repo guidance. The engine mechanically refuses closeout (c4) when the staged diff includes suspicious artifacts (oversized files, generated record dumps, disallowed dirs, binary/blob additions, large data files); if any are intentional, a human waives c4 via <engine> waive archive --cond c4 --authority human --reason "..." rather than hand-editing the spine. Release the engine session lease only as your VERY LAST action, AFTER the archive postconditions pass and you have run the engine's final advance on archive (the advance that marks the spine done): by default call the spine_lease MCP tool with action=release (this is your own spine; the door needs no session id argument). CLI fallback: <engine> release --session-id commander-epic-567-door/cmdr-a. Release must come after that closing advance, never before it — the lease must cover every journaled action, so the release is the final journal entry; releasing earlier leaves archive's own closeout entries (attest/waive/advance) after the lease release and fails the terminal provenance check.

postconditions.statement: work area archived and this run's episode captured AND tracked by git, so the record survives this worktree
branch committed and pushed

the work is REACHABLE: this branch has a pull request that is OPEN or MERGED. A merged PR is reachable work; a closed-unmerged one is not, and neither is no PR at all. A terminal spine and a pushed branch describe the run, not the ref -- CI never runs on an unopened branch, and every commander that reached a terminal spine without opening one had to be chased for it. Open the PR even if the work is unfinished; declare FINAL or PENDING in its title and hand the merge up. Two properties of the check text are load-bearing. The branch is derived at CHECK time from the repo root, never resolved at instantiation: init instantiates the spine before it starts the branch, so the branch need not exist yet -- and a literal branch placeholder is not a resolver-owned token, so instantiation cannot catch one and would ship it unsubstituted. The count is compared in the SHELL because the engine's verdict for a command condition is the EXIT CODE and stdout is discarded: gh --jq 'length > 0' prints true or false but exits 0 either way, so that form can never fail.

check.command: test "$(gh pr list --head "$(git -C /home/tommy/projects/constellation-skills/.worktrees/567-a-spine-identity rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" --state all --json state --jq '[.[] | select(.state == "OPEN" or .state == "MERGED")] | length')" -gt 0

why_trail.why: Bootstrap complete in the assigned worktree (feat/567-a-spine-identity, isolation verified exit 0). Work area and spine instantiated from the commander template; lease cmdr-567-a active. Two bootstrap findings already recorded in notes-a.md: the launch order's engine path (constellation-commander-delegated/scripts/) does not exist and the real engine is the constellation-commander copy; and the door REFUSES every tool because no spine is bound to this process, which is this lane's own anchor defect reproduced on step one.

Doctrine and project deltas read; map is DEGRADED repo-wide and discharged with substitutes, so my frame for the door/engine identity area comes from the previous lane A's own prose in notes-a.md, which settles decision:bind-on-open-over-new-verb and names the two AST pins in tests/test_mcp_lifecycle.py constraining where a rebind may sit. Three findings already recorded: the bind-own-spine gap is reproduced in my own process (F1); the entire mechanism to fix it already exists in mcp_spine_server.py and only a second caller of _bind_process_to is missing (F2); checklist_engine.save() is a bare write_bytes with no atomic replace (F3). Also recorded that my own assigned notes file was another lane's committed artifact, which I clobbered and restored with zero lines lost (L1).

Problem statement written and reconciled against the frozen order. The defect is one missing verb, not a missing mechanism: _bind_process_to already exists as the single named rebinder with a module-wide AST pin, all four import-time SPINE derivations are already late-bound, and _unbound_refusal is already asked per call rather than cached -- all shipped by the previous lane A under decision:bind-on-open-over-new-verb. Its only caller is _spine_open, which MINTS. Nothing binds the door to a spine that already exists. Second half confirmed independently: checklist_engine.save() ends in a bare write_bytes, so a torn read or a crash-corrupt spine is reachable; atomic replace fixes that but NOT lost updates, and I hold that boundary explicitly.

Plan frozen after a design-it-twice panel of 3 and a cold critic that returned 5 blocking findings. The recommendation is a named hybrid: candidate A's spine_bind tool with the session derived from the spine's work_id rather than origin.work_id -- because A's own stated falsifier, when I ran it, showed origin.work_id is absent from 92% of live spines including the Admiral's own and IMPLEMENTER_PLAN.json, the two cases the mission names. The critic then inverted my central argument: I had killed candidate C on a measured 683-file reach and crowned A on an unmeasured one that is actually 4205 with 3505 cross-worktree, because _primary_checkout_for_lifecycle resolves --git-common-dir. Root narrowed to <own checkout>/.agent-work via --show-toplevel plus a cross-checkout refusal: 683, cross-checkout 0. Also amended execute.json through the engine because every one of its command postconditions passed at base with zero code written; the new ones verifiably fail at base. Two implementer crews are running in parallel under file fences (g2 owns mcp_spine_server.py/spine_lifecycle.py, g3 owns checklist_engine.py).

Both mission halves shipped and independently verified. spine_bind gives any role a door path to a spine that already exists -- the defect that stopped the Admiral at init and put this lane on the epic's critical path -- and checklist_engine.save() is now atomic. The run's most valuable outputs were not the code: running the winning candidate's own falsifier showed its session derivation would have refused 92% of live spines including the two the mission names; a cold critic inverted my central reach argument with a measurement I had not taken; the implementing crew's own GREEN mutation revealed my security fix was structurally untestable because every fixture used a topology where both roots agree; and two independent reviewers found a symlink hole in the guard I had narrowed, after I had run six boundary attacks and declared it sound with not one symlink among them. PR #623 open, not merged.

Structural record reconciled directly (no packet map exists in this repo). The load-bearing fold is docs/CHECKLIST_ENGINE_DESIGN.md, which asserted the door cannot be pointed at another spine -- half-false after this lane, and the half that survives (identity is still never a tool argument) is the half worth keeping precise. Also recorded a claim I did NOT change: the schema's opened_by row, because binding does not open.

Eleven candidates routed recommend-and-defer, zero issues filed. The three highest-value ones came from crews and reviewers rather than from me, and the single most important is a measurement-integrity defect that undercuts every green-suite claim in this wave: four tests reporting PASSED while their bodies raised inside subTest. I flag it as outranking my own deliverables because mutation testing -- the technique that caught this lane's untestable containment root -- cannot see it, since the mutant is never evaluated.

RETURN.md is the run summary and opens with the human-facing block: the one design question with what turns on each answer, and the one weakness stated without softening. The design pick is deliberately left unratified. Also carries the isolation evidence, the design-it-twice comparison, the self-hosting proofs with their pre-edit baseline, the fresh-process validation with its stated limits, the deletion accounting, the touched-path list with a merge-collision flag on run_crew.py, PR #623, the eleven triage candidates, and a workflow-feedback section that names five of my own mistakes rather than only the tooling's.

Reflected honestly and recorded 12 episodes, one per distinct thing that happened, each a record rather than a rule. Three deviations disclosed at the time rather than at the end: crew dispatch bypassed run_crew.py (whose only in-harness backend refuses --spine, so it offers bookkeeping not a launch -- mitigated by verifying every crew's side-effects myself), two edits outside my file ownership that were mechanically required and are flagged as a merge collision, and the c6 waiver which I did not let buy me out of the underlying property. Crew feedback harvested: all five crews independently named 'a green suite is not evidence' as the handoff's most valuable line, and the subTest measurement-integrity defect one of them found outranks my own deliverables.
